Thanks again for the time yesterday. I've attached the draft order form (orderform_v3.pdf) with the pricing schedule we discussed. Quick summary to make sure we're aligned:

- Annual committed spend: $600k (tiered pricing; see Appendix).
- Minimum commit: $150k/year (billed quarterly in arrears).
- Invoicing cadence: quarterly invoices (QTR usage + any overage) with line-item breakdown by SKU.
- Default net terms proposed: Net 45.

A couple of open items we flagged for Procurement:
1) Invoice recipient/entity — your team mentioned an EU operating company; please confirm legal entity name and billing address to put on the order form.
2) Taxes — do you require Redwood to register locally or do you anticipate reverse-charge/VAT handling on your side? If you have a VAT certificate, send it and we’ll attach it to the order.
3) Withholding — is there any local withholding requirement we should account for in pricing?

Could you loop in Procurement/Finance and confirm the invoice entity + desired net terms? If Net 30 is required for EU, we can propose a split invoice approach but need Legal/Finance to weigh in.

Next steps: once you confirm entity and any PO number, I'll get Legal/Finance to produce a short amendment (Appendix A) that captures the invoicing split & tax allocation so we can DocuSign.

Attachments: orderform_v3.pdf (PDF, draft)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks. A couple quick clarifications from Procurement/Tax:

- Invoicing entity: ClearWave Technologies EMEA Ltd (UK address); we also have a US parent for global billing.
- VAT: ClearWave will apply reverse-charge where applicable; I attached our VAT cert for the EMEA entity (clearwave_tax_certificate.pdf).
- Withholding: we do not typically withhold VAT, but some local teams have withholding obligations on certain services — procurement will confirm if this applies to the pilot.
- Net terms: our standard is Net 30 for EMEA entities. We can accept Net 45 in exceptional cases, but Procurement will push for Net 30.

If Redwood prefers consolidated billing to the US parent, we can consider, but Procurement will need to know how tax credits / VAT reclaim will work.

Please let me know if Redwood can: A) issue separate invoices to EMEA entity for VAT purposes, or B) issue consolidated invoice to US parent with VAT evidence so we can reclaim.

Thanks —

Kimberly / Ben —

Forwarding ClearWave's response. High level asks they want to resolve before signature:

1) Invoice entity: ClearWave Technologies EMEA Ltd (UK) — they'd like VAT reverse-charge handled and Net 30 for EMEA.
2) Option to consolidate to US parent if Redwood can provide evidence that allows VAT reclaim.
3) Potential local withholding on pilot — procurement will confirm.

My suggested commercial compromises:
- Add Appendix A to the order form that allows per-quarter invoice allocation by entity (Redwood to invoice nominated entity for a % split) OR consolidated invoicing to a nominated parent if customer provides tax reclaim evidence.
- Accept Net 30 for the EMEA entity only; retain Net 45 for consolidated US invoices.
- Add tax responsibility clause: customer responsible for VAT/withholding; Redwood will provide VAT invoices and evidence where applicable.

Can you confirm if Finance is OK with split invoices (we'd need to route revenue accordingly) and Legal if language below is acceptable for the order form amendment: "Seller will invoice the billing entity nominated on the Order Form; taxes (VAT, withholding) are the responsibility of the purchasing entity unless otherwise agreed in writing. For cross-entity consolidated invoices, Customer will provide documentation enabling recovery of local VAT and Redwood will not assume withholding liability."

If you can provide a quick redline this morning I can send back to Sana and move to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sana Ahmed <sana.ahmed@clearwave.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commercial settlement: pricing schedule & invoice routing — proposed language and routing

Jordan / Sana —

Legal + Finance response consolidated below. We reviewed the draft and propose the following practical language and operational approach so we can sign without opening broader tax exposure: 

1) Invoice entity and split invoicing
- Redwood will invoice the legal entity named on the Order Form. If Customer nominates multiple purchasing entities, Redwood will invoice each nominated entity for the agreed allocation in Appendix A. Appendix A will list the per-quarter allocation percentages and invoice remit addresses.

2) Net terms
- Net 30 will apply only to invoices issued to EU/EMEA entities where Customer provides valid VAT registration and contact. Consolidated invoices issued to a US parent will be Net 45 by default.

3) Taxes & withholding
- Customer is responsible for all taxes, duties and withholding under applicable law. If Customer withholds any amounts, they must provide written evidence and gross-up where required by local law. Redwood will provide VAT invoices and supporting documentation to enable Customer's reclaim. Redwood will not register for or assume responsibility for Customer's local tax withholding obligations.

4) Operational notes (Finance)
- Finance confirms we can support split invoicing by entity; we require a signed Appendix A and PO numbers to map invoices correctly. Redline attached: redline_orderform_v3.pdf (contains Appendix A template and proposed clause language).

Action items:
- Jordan: please confirm with ClearWave if they accept Appendix A approach and submit PO numbers for the nominated entities.
- Sana: if you confirm Appendix A and provide PO for ClearWave EMEA and (optionally) US parent, we'll prepare DocuSign package.

If ClearWave wants Redwood to issue a single consolidated invoice to the US parent and expects Redwood to facilitate VAT reclaim, we need a separate tax agreement and it's out of scope for the standard order form.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
